body.input: Which companies opened an office in the Netherlands in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, the following companies opened an office or significantly expanded their presence in the Netherlands in 2026:

1. **EGT** — Opened a new office in **'s-Hertogenbosch (Den Bosch)** on **May 13, 2026**, as part of its expansion into the Dutch iGaming market.

2. **Databricks** — Moved into a new 13,000 m² office spanning eleven floors in **Amsterdam's The Rock tower** (announced November 2026), as part of a $500 million+ investment in the Netherlands over three years. The company is expanding its largest European R&D hub and plans to double its local team.

3. **Alibaba Cloud** — Opened its **first public cloud region in the Netherlands** with two data centres in **Amsterdam** (November 12, 2026), marking its fourth cloud region in Europe.

4. **Oko Camera** (Ukrainian defense tech company) — Opened a company in **Eindhoven** (announced November 12, 2026), including plans to set up production of combat thermal cameras in the Netherlands.

5. **Robin Radar Systems** — Opened a **new headquarters in Delft** (November 12, 2026), officially opened by the King of the Netherlands, with a speech by Minister Derk Boswijk.

6. **Fresha** — Opened a new office in the Netherlands (announced February 2025) as part of its European expansion into Madrid, Paris, and the Netherlands.

This list reflects publicly reported office openings and may not be exhaustive.

# Alibaba Cloud opens first Dutch public cloud region

 Thu, 12th Nov 2026 (Today)

Shadda Lie Catugal

SHADDA LIE CATUGAL  Editor

Alibaba Cloud has opened its first public cloud region in the Netherlands, with two data centres in Amsterdam.

The launch gives Alibaba Cloud a fourth cloud region in Europe, after Frankfurt, London and Paris, extending its local infrastructure footprint as European customers look to keep data and AI workloads within the region. [...] "We are pleased to partner with Alibaba and integrate its advanced AI models into Magnific. This collaboration strengthens our platform and gives creators more powerful tools to accelerate their work and expand their creative possibilities," Florido said.

"We are committed to making great creative tools accessible to everyone, and Alibaba Cloud's advanced AI models help us deliver that at scale in a cost-effective way. This is just the start; we're excited to deepen the collaboration across the whole creative industry," Hillenaar said.

European build-out

The Netherlands region is part of a wider expansion in Europe and sits within a broader infrastructure programme announced by Alibaba. The new site brings its global estate to 109 availability zones across 32 regions. [...] "The Netherlands is one of Europe's most vibrant digital economies, and our first region here is a direct response to the strong demand we see from local businesses building and scaling with AI. By bringing our advanced AI and cloud capabilities to Amsterdam, we are giving customers the in-region infrastructure, performance and data residency they need to innovate faster, scale securely and operate with greater efficiency in the AI era," Dr Li said.

Customer links

Alibaba Cloud also highlighted several companies using its AI models and cloud services in Europe, including a cluster of customers in the Netherlands.

# Speech by Minister Derk Boswijk at the opening of Robin Radar Systems' new headquarters

Speech12-11-2026

Ladies and gentlemen, dear Robins,

A radar exists to pick up a signal. Today, Robin Radar Systems is sending out a signal of its own.  
 You have moved to a wonderful new home, or in your own words: a new nest.  
 The King himself just opened this building.  
 That shows how much Robin Radar means to the Netherlands. [...] I cannot comment on the sale process.  
 But let me share my personal expectation.  
 Your roots lie in Dutch research. You work closely with our armed forces and those of our allies.  
 So I expect Robin Radar to stay firmly grounded in the Netherlands and in the Dutch innovation ecosystem.  
 This new headquarters in Delft is a sign of that intention.

It brings me back to what your radars do every day. A radar buys time.  
 In Ukraine, that time saves lives. At home, it protects our bases.

The faster we build together, the more time we win.  
 Industry, Defence and research working as one.  
 That is how Siete and his Robins built a European leader.  
 And that is the signal you are sending today.

Congratulations on your new nest. Let’s make every minute count.

Thank you. [...] Your radars are a prime example. They bring together sensors and air defence.  
 In sensors, and radar in particular, our country is a world leader.  
 Defence makes extra investments in that area.  
 And air and missile defence is a top priority.

Before I close, one last word about Robin Radar itself.  
 In this new nest, you can build more radars, close to TNO and TU Delft.  
 Growth on this scale needs capital. That calls for investors, possibly from abroad.  
 So you are also entering a new phase in ownership.
